_notes: B2 — Crew move and job change, office half (catalog B2, plan test-plans/journey-b/b02-crew-move-and-job-change.md, recording docs/media/Journey B2 Crew Move and Job Change.mp4, runner row B2-001). After the supervisor moves the crew mid-day, the office must show each mover in the destination field/job and the member left behind still in the original.

Four rows, not seven: a move on the device is not a second punch — each mover's existing Time In is updated in place, same row and same reference, and no time-out is written. The device therefore exports the crew's FINAL state, which is what these records are: movers 6001/6002/6003 in field2 4102 / job2 4202, member 6004 left behind in field 4101 / job 4201. One punch per crew member — a move reassigns, it never adds.
Device-side proof of that behaviour needs the app itself and is parked with the mobile automation; this file covers the office side.

dayOffset -1: B1 and B2 share crew members and run in parallel workers against the same tenant; punching the same day would trip the office's duplicate-Time-In rule and flip the rows from Warning to Blocking, so B2 lives on yesterday and keeps both grids disjoint. punchTime 07:15 is the crew envelope's single punch moment.

expected.envelope.fields/jobs replace the old '<Field>4102</Field>' / '<Job>4202</Job>' string greps. expected.cards[0] (panel: true) is the Time In panel's candidate — the post-move destination display names come from fixture.json (field2 'B2 FIELD EAST', job2 'B2 PRUNING').

cleanup: the timeCards step sweeps the four crew members' fixture day before the import (what verifyImportInOffice's default sweep did) and deletes the imported cards after the test; the flow passes sweep:false so exactly one cleanup path is live.
